cases.exposure_context_quote: A 22-year-old male was brought to the Emergency Department (ED) by relatives with a history of consuming about 100 ml of a chemical about one and a half hours back in an attempt to commit suicide.
cases.agent: deltamethrin 12.5 mg/mL, around 100 mL (brand advertised as anti-tick animal medication)
cases.agent_quote: He had consumed around 100 ml of deltamethrin 12.5 mg per ml.
cases.circumstance: suicidal attempt; ingested about 100 ml of an unknown chemical about one and a half hours before ED arrival

symptoms.quote: He has had about 10 episodes of vomiting since then.

symptoms.finding: fasciculations of calf muscles (lasted about 30 minutes since arrival)
symptoms.quote: There were fasciculations of his calf muscles and a smell resembling the smell of organophosphate compounds.
There were fasciculations of his calf muscles and a smell resembling the smell of organophosphate compounds.
vitals were as follows: pulse rate: 102 per minute, blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg, respiratory rate: 16 per minute, temperature: 97.5 °F, and oxygen saturation: 100% on room air.

cases.time_to_care: brought to ED about one and a half hours after ingestion

labs.name: complete blood counts, kidney and liver function tests, coagulation profile, ECG
labs.quote: His complete blood counts, kidney and liver function tests, coagulation profile, and electrocardiogram (ECG) were within normal limits.

labs.name: serum cholinesterase
labs.quote: Serum cholinesterase levels were also normal.

treatment.name: atropine challenge test (1 mg atropine; positive, HR rose from 105 to 152/min)
treatment.quote: an atropine challenge test was done with 1 mg of atropine. The test was positive, with the heart rate rising from 105 per minute to 152 per minute.

treatment.name: atropine 2 mg (minimal dose, as for OP poisoning)
treatment.quote: the patient was started on a minimal dose of 2 mg atropine

treatment.name: pralidoxime 30 mg/kg in 100 ml normal saline over 20 minutes (stopped, almost fully infused)
treatment.quote: starting dose of 30 mg per kg pralidoxime in 100 ml normal saline over 20 minutes as per routine treatment followed for organophosphate compound poisoning

treatment.name: supportive treatment: pantoprazole and intravenous fluids
treatment.quote: He was admitted to the intensive care unit and was conservatively treated with pantoprazole and intravenous fluids.

treatment.name: escitalopram and clonazepam (psychiatric)
treatment.quote: He was discharged on the fourth day with escitalopram and clonazepam prescribed by the psychiatrist.

cases.outcome: no complications; discharged on the fourth day
cases.outcome_quote: There were no complications during his four-day stay in the hospital... He was discharged on the fourth day with escitalopram and clonazepam prescribed by the psychiatrist.
cases.sequelae: none; diagnosed with depression disorder by psychiatrist
cases.notes: Initially treated empirically as organophosphate poisoning until compound identified as deltamethrin; first report of a positive atropine challenge test with deltamethrin.
